scenario.title: Ten minutes before you start
scenario.intro: You are about to learn the CIMMYT MEAL Framework 2026–2030 in about five hours of self-paced study. Before the first module, three short lessons show you how the course works, preview every concept in ninety seconds, and let you pick the examples that match your role. None of this is assessed.

objectives.text: Describe how the diagnostic, personal plan, mastery checks and certificate fit together.
Name the ten module concepts in the order the framework presents them.

lessons.title: How this course works: diagnostic, plan, mastery checks, certificate

beats.hook: You do not have to study everything. The course first finds out what you already know, then tells you what to skip as clearly as what to study.

example.title: What a plan looks like
body: A field officer takes the 15-question diagnostic and taps Sure or Not sure after each answer. She misses a foundation question on KPIs and a scenario question on accountability, and she is unsure about her correct answer on impact.

Her plan says: Start here for KPIs & measurement (the full module, 40 minutes). Review for Accountability & inclusion, starting at lesson 9.2. Check first for Impact assessment (take the 5-question check, study only if needed). Everything else is Looking good, optional.
About 1 h 10 min to close her gaps. She passes the KPI check at 4 out of 5, the module stamps Mastered and the plan shrinks. Seven days later the home page offers a 3-question refresher.

bullets: Diagnostic first. Then a plan that names modules and the lessons inside them, with a reason for each.
A module is mastered when you pass its 5-question check at 80%. Watching lessons is never required to unlock a check.
All ten modules mastered plus the capstone unlocks the completion certificate.

source.title: A New MEAL Approach for CIMMYT

beats.hook: Ten modules, one logic: why evidence changes, what the results chain is, how to measure, how to manage data, how to claim impact, how to learn and account for it, and how to run it all.

example.title: The ten modules, in the framework's own order
body: Why: M1 MEAL foundations. What: M2 Theory of change, M3 Results framework. How to measure: M4 KPIs & measurement. How to manage data: M5 Data quality & collection, M6 Evidence & data systems.
How to claim impact: M7 Impact assessment. How to learn and account: M8 Learning & adaptation, M9 Accountability & inclusion. How to run it: M10 Implementation & governance.
Every module is self-standing. The order is a recommendation, not a gate.

bullets: The framework moves from reports to observation-level evidence so CIMMYT can say what changed, for whom, where and what it contributed.
Four results levels, five evidence functions, one KPI toolbox, one data system, four directions of accountability.
Modules map one to one to the ten diagnostic topics.

beats.hook: A project lead and a data officer need different examples. Tell the course who you are and the scenarios will lean your way.

example.title: Choose the role closest to yours
example.prompt: Your choice tunes which scenarios and examples the course highlights. You can change it any time from this lesson.

bullets: Your persona changes emphasis, not content. Every lesson is open to everyone.
The plan, not the module order, decides what the course suggests next.
Nothing is locked. Open any module, lesson or check whenever you want.

source.title: MEAL in the Context of CIMMYT

frames.narration: Start with the diagnostic: fifteen questions, one per topic plus a second in five of them. After each answer, tap Sure or Not sure.

scene.title: Diagnostic first
scene.subtitle: 15 questions. Sure or Not sure after each.

frames.narration: Your answers become a plan. Modules land in one of four bands: Start here, Review, Check first or Looking good, each with a reason and the first lesson to open.

Each module ends with a five-question mastery check. Four out of five passes. Pass, and the module stamps Mastered and leaves your plan. Miss, and the plan lists the lessons for what you missed and offers a fresh draw.
The plan shrinks as checks are passed. When all ten modules are mastered and the capstone is done, you can print a completion certificate. No score on it, only completed.
Seven and thirty days after mastering a module, the home page offers a three-question refresher. Everything stays in your browser. Export your learning record whenever you like.

scene.log: Spaced re-checks keep what you learned

frames.narration: Why change? Reports can say what was delivered. They cannot show what changed on the ground. The framework builds evidence from observations instead.
Evidence is organised along a results chain: processes, outputs, outcomes and impact. A theory of change says how each link is expected to lead to the next, and under which assumptions.

Measurement runs through one KPI toolbox: 142 indicators in 13 volumes under three Thrusts. One KPI can be measured at several levels with different valid methods, and institutional totals are recomputed from records, never summed from reports.

Data quality has six dimensions. The evidence stack combines direct observations, earth observation, context data and operational records in one data system that collects data once and reports many times.

Impact claims are about contribution, not sole cause, and they need a credible counterfactual. Learning runs on a cadence of evidence reviews and decision logs. Accountability runs in four directions.

And it all runs through a project lifecycle with gates, a MEAL Matrix that classifies and budgets every project, and a lean MEAL team. By 2030 the question changes from what did we do to what changed, for whom, and what did CIMMYT contribute.

scene.title: What changed, for whom, and what did CIMMYT contribute?
scene.subtitle: The question the framework is built to answer by 2030.

frames.narration: Five kinds of people take this course. A project lead needs budgets and requirements. A data officer needs quality rules. A scientist needs the case for observation-level evidence.
Pick the one closest to your work. The course keeps every lesson open to everyone and only changes which examples it leads with.

scene.subtitle: Examples lean your way. Nothing is hidden.
